title: Frost
description: A model and execution-profile recommender: task analysis in, one deterministic Recommend policy, human or JSON out.
provenance: Updated on 2026-09-16 from the Go sources under cmd/, internal/ and tools/catalog-build after slices 1, 1a and 2 were implemented, plus config/ and examples/capacity. Only evaluation and the later API/MCP adapters remain proposed. Current public data still provides no applicable task-family measurements for the configured models, and no paired completion-outcome evaluation exists; the diagram describes implemented boundaries, not recommendation quality. Evidence paths are pointers into this repository, not proof that a claim is still current.

boundaries.title: Deterministic core
boundaries.description: No environment, filesystem or network reads. Adapters produce the inputs and render the Decision.

boundaries.title: Public model evidence
boundaries.description: Neutral, source-attributed facts about models. Frost reads the file; a producer, not the router, knows the separately licensed sources.

boundaries.title: Operator-owned configuration
boundaries.description: What the operator can actually run and how to choose: profiles, labeled priors, latency classes, policy, pools, and the question set the analyzer is asked.

boundaries.title: Transient capacity
boundaries.description: Ephemeral usage observations, produced outside Frost and read as a neutral snapshot. A snapshot cannot redefine profile-to-pool topology.

boundaries.title: Route-time network seam
boundaries.description: Task text leaves the route here and nowhere else. Catalog and capacity producers have separate source-specific network boundaries and never receive task text.

boundaries.title: Explicit local records
boundaries.description: Recording is opt-in with --record because the record stores task text. Replay recomputes the policy from stored answers.

scenes.title: The big picture
scenes.description: The frost CLI and separate catalog producer around one pure selection core, with operator-owned files and an optional external capacity producer.

scenes.title: One route, start to finish
scenes.description: A task enters through the CLI, optional capacity is loaded, the task is judged by the analyzer, Recommend applies adequacy before availability and expiry, and the result is rendered; --record keeps the answers and --replay recomputes without the provider.

scenes.title: Inside Recommend
scenes.description: How a validated assessment becomes a Decision inside the pure core: read distributions, apply hard constraints, decide adequacy from measurements or labeled priors, then order by objective, availability, expiring included usage, cost and stable ID. Capacity cannot raise the quality floor.

scenes.title: Who owns each input
scenes.description: Public model evidence, operator-owned configuration and transient capacity observations are separate inputs with separate owners; the router only sees their normalized types.

scenes.title: What remains proposed
scenes.description: Planned, not built: reproducible paired-outcome evaluation (slice 3) and later API and MCP adapters over the same Recommend boundary.
